title: Single-sample deployment with OmicSelector
text: Deployment problem. Classical batch-aware corrections ComBat, quantile normalization, RUV designed around batch reference set. mismatch clinical-style handoff one new specimen arrives alone must scored without co-resident test samples. Honest caveat. value API deployability: scores one incoming specimen panel values plus frozen fit-time parameters, co-resident test batch. claim ws-balance-ilr, single-sample method, -discriminates batch-corrected pipeline — choose validate scoring method data.

what: Make a tiny synthetic compositional panel
title: Single-sample deployment with OmicSelector
text: vignette uses self-contained synthetic count-like matrix. feature names come default within-sample balance dictionary example exercises panel shape deployment tests, data downloaded.
code: set.seed(101)  sbp <- ws_default_sbp() sentinels <- c("ALL_NON_RBC", "ALL_NON_PLT",                "TOP_K_BY_ABUNDANCE", "TAIL_BY_ABUNDANCE") features <- unique(unlist(lapply(sbp, function(balance) {   c(balance$numerator, balance$denominator) }), use.names = FALSE)) features <- features[!features %in% sentinels] features <- features[seq_len(30L)]  n <- 40L y <- rep(c(0L, 1L), each = n / 2L) X <- matrix(   stats::rgamma(n * length(features), shape = 20, rate = 2),   nrow = n,   dimnames = list(paste0("S", seq_len(n)), features) ) X[y == 1L, features[1:5]] <- X[y == 1L, features[1:5]] + 80 X[y == 0L, features[6:10]] <- X[y == 0L, features[6:10]] + 80  holdout <- nrow(X) X_train <- X[-holdout, , drop = FALSE] y_train <- y[-holdout] x_new <- X[holdout, , drop = FALSE]  dim(X_train) #> [1] 39 30 dim(x_new) #> [1]  1 30

what: Fit once, then freeze the scorer
title: Single-sample deployment with OmicSelector
text: deploy_singlesample() fits one rostered method stores frozen model state needed future singleton scoring. default ws-balance-ilr method compositional deployment default, certified benchmark winner.
code: dep <- deploy_singlesample(   X_train,   y_train,   method = "ws-balance-ilr" )  print(dep) #> OmicSelector single-sample deployable #>   method_id: ws-balance-ilr #>   n_train: 39 #>   gate: verified row-equivariant scoring on 39 probe rows (single specimen == same row in batch; frozen model) #>   caveat: deployability only; not a claim of superior discrimination over a batch-corrected pipeline.

title: Single-sample deployment with OmicSelector
text: score_specimen() needs held-specimen row frozen deployment object. test batch, co-resident reference cohort, test-time batch correction supplied.
code: score <- score_specimen(dep, x_new) score #> [1] 8.42726

title: Single-sample deployment with OmicSelector
text: deployability gate checks property needed singleton use: specimen’s score computed alone computed row batch, frozen model unchanged.
code: is_singlesample_deployable(dep, X_probe = X_train) #> [1] TRUE

what: Inspect the method roster, not a ranking
title: Single-sample deployment with OmicSelector
text: deployment wrapper intentionally fail-closed. Roughly 30 rostered single-sample methods deployable fit-freeze-score pattern, methods needing cohort context, unavailable backends, non-scalar outputs reject cleanly rather pretending singleton-safe. Use singlesample_method_roster() inspect current roster treat roster order performance ranking. deployability contract roster guarantees, ranking: deployable method can score one incoming specimen without new batch test-time batch-correction step. certify method provides superior discrimination, benchmark method choice cohorts.
code: roster <- singlesample_method_roster() head(roster[, c("method_id", "tier", "dep_route")], 8) #>             method_id tier dep_route #> 1     ws-rclr-trimmed   R1    base-R #> 2        ws-alr-pivot   R1    base-R #> 3     ws-mad-logratio   R1    base-R #> 4        ws-dominance   R1    base-R #> 5          frozen-ruv   R1    base-R #> 6    robust-pca-resid   R1    base-R #> 7     hemolysis-resid   R1    base-R #> 8 kit-stratified-rclr   R1    base-R

title: Hurdle Filter for Zero-Inflated Data — FilterHurdle

text: OmicSelector 2.6.0 toolkit high-dimensional biomarker discovery leakage-resistant validation, stable feature selection, within-sample panel methods, frozen-reference denoising add-ons, qPCR non-detect handling, matched-null benchmarks, provenance-aware audit helpers.

title: OmicSelector: Zero-Leakage Biomarker Discovery Toolkit — OmicSelector-package
text: ## Key Features - **Zero Data Leakage**: preprocessing, feature selection, model training   occurs within proper cross-validation folds via mlr3 GraphLearners. - **Nested Cross-Validation**: Inner loop feature selection hyperparameter   tuning, outer loop unbiased performance estimation. - **Stability Metrics**: Nogueira Stability Index ensure selected features   robust across resamples, just high accuracy. - **Reproducibility**: renv lockfiles, Docker containers, deterministic pipelines. - **Panel Governance**: Group-aware resampling, provenance-floor diagnostics,   identifiability gates, matched-null benchmarks, operating-point summaries   biomarker panels evaluated public omics data. ## Core Classes - [OmicPipeline]: Central R6 class creating leakage-free pipelines - [BenchmarkService]: Enforces proper nested cross-validation ## Quick Start “`r library(OmicSelector) # Create pipeline data pipeline <- OmicPipeline$new(   data = my_data,   target = "outcome",   positive = "Case" ) # Create graph learner feature selection learner <- pipeline$create_graph_learner(   filter = "anova",   model = "ranger",   n_features = 20 ) # Run nested CV benchmark service <- BenchmarkService$new(pipeline, outer_folds = 5, inner_folds = 3) service$add_learner(learner) result <- service$run() “` ## Philosophy OmicSelector 2.6.0 prioritizes leakage-resistant validation, feature stability, auditable provenance checks raw apparent accuracy. High accuracy unstable feature sets strong provenance-prediction treated warning signal rather direct biomarker evidence.

title: Hybrid Sequential Feature Selection (HSFS) — SequentialSelector
text: Implements multi-stage feature reduction pipeline handle high-dimensional omics data efficiently. pipeline chains: 1. Variance thresholding (remove near-zero variance) 2. Univariate filtering (ANOVA F-test) 3. RF importance filtering (single-pass, iterative RFE) 4. AUC filter final selection (univariate ranking AUC) Note: RF importance stage single-pass approximation using Random Forest variable importance, true iterative Recursive Feature Elimination. final stage uses univariate AUC filtering (LASSO regularization). hybrid approach outperforms single-method selection high-dimensional data.

title: Stability-Based Ensemble Selection — StabilityEnsemble
text: Builds ensemble models using stability-based feature selection. approach: 1. Run N bootstrap resamples feature selection 2. Compute feature selection frequencies 3. Create nested overlapping subsets based stability tiers 4. Train K base models different stability tiers 5. Combine predictions via stability-weighted voting approach addresses "reproducibility crisis" biomarker discovery prioritizing stable, reproducible feature sets single-run selections.

what: Fit unconstrained least-squares importance-fitting (uLSIF) density-ratio LRT — fit_dre_ulsif
title: Fit unconstrained least-squares importance-fitting (uLSIF) density-ratio LRT — fit_dre_ulsif
text: Learns frozen two-class discriminator training data directly estimating class-conditional density ratio \(w(x) = p_{\mathrm{case}}(x) / p_{\mathrm{control}}(x)\) – without ever estimating either density – using unconstrained Least-Squares Importance Fitting (uLSIF; Kanamori, Hido & Sugiyama 2009). estimated ratio Neyman-Pearson-optimal class-conditional likelihood ratio, larger \(w(z)\) means case-like. specimen first mapped self-contained, per-sample robust centred-log-ratio (rCLR) representation \(z\), \(z_j = \log v_j - \mathrm{mean}_{k:\,v_k>0}\log v_k\) nonzero parts specimen \(z_j = 0\) zero parts. centring uses specimen's nonzero values, \(z(c\,v) = z(v)\) \(c>0\): representation – therefore every downstream score – exactly invariant per-sample scaling (library size / input amount). density ratio modelled non-negative combination Gaussian basis functions \(\phi_l(z) = \exp(-\lVert z - c_l\rVert^2 / (2\sigma^2))\) centred \(b\) frozen kernel centres \(c_l\). centres deterministic frozen subsample case rCLR anchors (cap hp$n_centers); bandwidth \(\sigma\) either supplied hp$sigma learned median heuristic pairwise Euclidean distances among centres. Writing \(\Phi_{\mathrm{control}}\) \(\Phi_{\mathrm{case}}\) kernel matrices control / case anchors centres, closed-form uLSIF coefficients solve ridge-regularized normal equations $$(H + \lambda )\,\alpha = h,\qquad       H = \tfrac{1}{n_{\mathrm{control}}}           \Phi_{\mathrm{control}}^\top \Phi_{\mathrm{control}},\qquad       h = \mathrm{colMeans}(\Phi_{\mathrm{case}}),$$ non-negative parts \(\alpha \leftarrow \max(\alpha, 0)\) kept \(\hat w(z) = \sum_l \alpha_l \phi_l(z) \ge 0\) valid density ratio. iteration: \(H\) Gram matrix (positive semidefinite), \(H + \lambda \) positive definite \(\lambda>0\) single linear solve exact (increase--positive-definite ridge loop guards pathological numerical rank deficiency). Fitting stores raw case/control anchor rows raw centre rows (kernel model can re-derived consistently present-feature subset scoring), frozen training feature universe, resolved hyperparameters, – inspection tests – full-universe representation (centers, sigma, alpha). test data test-time batch statistic used.

text: Learns frozen logistic discriminator subset robust-CLR (rCLR) features PREDICTIVE label INVARIANT (cohort-stable) across training environments (cohorts) named meta_train[[cohort_col]], following Invariant Causal Prediction (ICP) principle Peters, Buhlmann & Meinshausen (2016): predictor whose conditional relationship label INVARIANT across environments plausible (batch-robust, transferable) causal signal, whereas predictor whose effect VARIES cohort signals confounding / non-causal, batch-driven association dropped. makes fit_icp transfer-estimand method TRAINING (selection uses cross-environment structure), deployment fully SINGLE-SAMPLE: frozen model linear logistic score selected features evaluated one specimen's rCLR vector. transfer aspect entirely SELECTION. icp structural twin fit_sel_stablemate ONE change: feature-SELECTION step. sel-stablemate calls StableMate's predictivity+stability bootstrap ensembles, icp selects features explicit, tractable per-feature ICP invariance screen: PREDICTIVITY screen: pooled marginal logistic     glm(y ~ rclr_j, binomial) training rows; feature \(j\)     PREDICTIVE Wald p-value slope \(< \alpha_{pred}\)     (default 0.05). INVARIANCE screen (ICP core): per-cohort marginal logistic     glm(y ~ rclr_j, binomial) WITHIN VALID cohort (\(\ge 1\)     case \(\ge 1\) control \(\ge\) min_env_n rows), giving     per-cohort slopes \(b_j^{(e)}\) standard errors \(SE_e\).     cross-cohort HOMOGENEITY \(\{b_j^{(e)}\}\) tested Cochran's     fixed-effect heterogeneity statistic \(Q = \sum_e w_e (b_e -     \bar{b})^2\), \(w_e = 1/SE_e^2\), \(\bar{b} = \sum_e w_e b_e / \sum_e     w_e\), \(Q \sim \chi^2_{E-1}\) homogeneity. Feature \(j\)     INVARIANT Q p-value \(> \alpha_{inv}\) (default 0.10) —     .e. FAIL reject homogeneity, \(y \mid x_j\) relationship     stable across cohorts. SELECT feature \(j\) PREDICTIVE INVARIANT. frozen glm(y ~ ., binomial) fit rCLR SELECTED features, pooled training rows, intercept + per-feature coefficients stored. per-cohort glm sweep can touch RNG deterministic IRLS (), whole fit nevertheless wrapped global-.Random.seed save/restore guard set.seed(hp$seed) inside , fitting deterministic leaves caller's RNG state byte-unchanged — mirroring sel-stablemate contract. DEGENERATION (icp ALWAYS produces usable, non-empty head): meta_train NULL, cohort column missing,     \(< 2\) VALID cohorts, invariance screen evaluated     selection degrades GRACEFULLY PREDICTIVITY-screen (pooled     marginal logistic alone). n_environments == 1L records     caller intends cross-cohort transfer can audit whether mis-wired     meta_train silently demoted transfer method pooled     predictivity-selection. n_environments > 1L means ICP     invariance screen ran. feature passes screens, selection RELAXES (documented     model$selection_mode): take -homogeneous (highest Q     p-value) among predictive features, top_k (default     min(5, n_predictive)); still empty (predictive feature     ), take single -predictive feature. guarantees usable     non-empty head keeping relaxation auditable. Unlike sel-stablemate (stability method honestly returns EMPTY set nothing stable), icp's brief mandates always-non-empty head; relaxation taken therefore recorded model$selection_mode rather left empty.

"fixed": pseudocount across features, given         value (default 1.0). Backward-compatible         log2(x + 1) convention. "epsilon": pseudocount = 1e-6 features. value Numeric scalar; pseudocount used method = "fixed". Ignored otherwise. Default 1.0.

what: Ratio Image CNN for Biomarker Panel Classification — ratio-image-cnn
title: Ratio Image CNN for Biomarker Panel Classification — ratio-image-cnn
text: Converts biomarker expression profiles pairwise log-ratio images classifies using convolutional neural network. encoding additive-shift-invariant log-space: per-sample additive constant applied uniformly across features cancels exactly pairwise difference pixel(,j) = log2(x_i) - log2(x_j). yields reference-cohort-free representation preserves within-sample relationships removing uniform sample-level offsets.

title: Ratio Image CNN for Biomarker Panel Classification — ratio-image-cnn
text: panel \(p\) biomarkers, sample becomes \(p \times p\) image pixel(,j) = log2(biomarker_i / biomarker_j). log-scale data simply difference \(x_i - x_j\). default CNN uses two 3x3 convolutions, adaptive average pooling 3x3, 64-unit dense layer dropout 0.3, sigmoid output head. torch backend used available. learner wrapper stores fitted torch module applies training-fold normalization new samples prediction.

title: Single-sample within-sample compositional methods (Module A, P1) — singlesample-within-sample
text: Five Module-within-sample compositional transforms introduced OmicSelector single-sample scoring bank. methods single-sample reference-cohort-free: sample normalised, scored, projected using panel values, requirement external training cohort exist deployment time. property makes within-sample methods suitable clinical translation: diagnostic test built primitives can deployed computing per-patient score patient's panel measurement, without re-fitting normalization population reference. Methods provided: ws_rclr_trimmed: robust trimmed centred log-ratio     optional zero-detection-convention; tolerant dominant     contaminating species (haemolysis miRNAs) small-head--pool     compositions typical plasma/serum miRNA panels. ws_balance_ilr: orthonormal isometric log-ratio     balances frozen sequential binary partition encoding circulating     miRNA biology (red-blood-cell vs rest, platelet vs rest, let-7 family     within-cluster, miR-17~92, miR-200, miR-371~373, dominant-vs-tail     abundance balance). ws_alr_pivot: additive log-ratio frozen     pivot pool putatively low-variance circulating miRNAs serving     geometric-mean denominator (anchors transformation     stable internal reference rather choosing single feature     denominator). ws_mad_logratio: median-centred log-ratio     optional per-sample MAD scaling; Aitchison-valid robust     descriptive transform downstream learners require     zero-sum compositional coordinates. ws_dominance_score: panel-internal scalar QC     dominance score reporting fraction total panel signal carried     top-K features; flags pre-analytical failures (haemolysis,     incomplete extraction) calibrated Tier R reference     distribution. Helper utilities provided alongside: ws_default_sbp returns curated v1 sequential-binary-partition tree circulating miRNA panels, ws_default_pivot_pool returns curated v1 ALR pivot pool (six low-variance miRNAs; miR-92a-3p excluded recent serum/plasma literature treats erythrocyte-derived).

title: Single-sample within-sample compositional methods (Module A, P1) — singlesample-within-sample
text: Background: circulating miRNA biomarkers proposed minimally invasive cancer markers 2008 (Mitchell et al., PNAS). intervening years clinically actionable cancer-screening test emerged source despite thousands "candidate panel" papers. reasons predominantly technical (batch effects, hemolysis contamination, lack standards, reference-cohort dependency, cross-cohort leakage, absence provenance/claim-gating) rather biological. five within-sample compositional methods target two failure modes directly: reference-cohort dependency (method scores single sample using panel values) contamination dominant erythrocyte-derived species (miR-451a, miR-486-5p, miR-16, miR-144-3p, miR-92a-3p - explicitly handled either exclusion rCLR centering subset dedicated balances SBP tree). Module one six modules OmicSelector v2.4 toolkit. modules - Module B (hemolysis correction), Module C (frozen batch correction), Module D (outlier detection conformal claim-gating), Module E (multi-cancer / domain generalisation), Module F (self-supervised pretraining ablation) - documented single-sample scoring bank per-module help pages.

what: Block-aware two-stage BH-FDR for specimen-shared cohort clusters — singlesample_bh_fdr_correct_blocked
title: Block-aware two-stage BH-FDR for specimen-shared cohort clusters — singlesample_bh_fdr_correct_blocked
text: Naïve BH-FDR within modality family treats specimen-shared cohorts (e.g., Toray clusters \(\sim 94.5\%\) specimen reuse) independent tests, anti-conservative due strongly correlated test statistics. function implements two-stage correction: Within provenance block, combine cohort-level p-values via     Fisher's chi-square statistic. Two reference distributions     reported side side: conservative reference: \(S/c\)         \(\chi^2_{2k}\); intentionally conservative; used         frozen benchmark's headline counts. textbook reference (Brown 1975 / Kost-McDermott 2002):         \(S/c\) \(\chi^2_{2k/c}\) \(df\) rescaled         inflation factor. Apply BH-FDR across block-level p-values, separately     reference. inflation factor \(c(k) = 1 + (k - 1)\rho\) \(k\) number cohorts block \(\rho\) assumed within-block correlation (default \(\rho = 0.25\) reproduces frozen benchmark's headline configuration).

what: Nogueira Stability Index for Feature Selection — stability
title: Nogueira Stability Index for Feature Selection — stability
text: Functions computing Nogueira Stability Index, measures consistency feature selection across cross-validation folds.

title: Nogueira Stability Index for Feature Selection — stability
text: Nogueira Stability Index preferred Jaccard/Kuncheva indices invariant number selected features. high stability (close 1) indicates features consistently selected across different training subsets, suggesting robust signal rather overfitting specific data splits. Formula: $$S = 1 - \frac{V}{V_0}$$ : - V = (1/p) * sum(pi_j * (1 - pi_j)) [observed variance] - V_0 = (k_bar/p) * (1 - k_bar/p) [expected variance random selection] - pi_j = selection frequency feature j - k_bar = average number selected features - p = total number candidate features

text: Functions within-sample normalization operate single sample's feature values. methods use population-level statistics — sample normalized independently using feature values — cancel specific classes per-sample nuisance variation WITHOUT reference cohort. title: Within-Sample Normalization for Biomarker Panels — within-sample
text: Within-sample normalization addresses one component batch-effect problem circulating biomarker diagnostics: per-sample nuisance variation (collection-site offset, loading amount, total-library scaling). Traditional normalization methods (quantile, ComBat, z-score) require reference population, impractical point--care diagnostics. Within-sample methods sidestep reference-cohort requirement specific, narrower invariance scope: ws_logratio / ws_ratio_image: additive-shift-invariant     log-space (equivalently, invariant multiplicative per-sample     factor applied UNIFORMLY across features raw space).     invariant gene-specific shifts non-linear platform response. ws_zscore: invariant affine per-sample transforms     (scale + shift) applied uniformly across features. ws_rank: invariant strictly monotonic per-sample     transform features. ws_minmax: invariant uniform per-sample affine transforms     sensitive outlier features. Available methods: ws_minmax: Scale sample's features [0,1] ws_rank: Replace values within-sample ranks ws_zscore: Standardize across features within sample ws_logratio: Compute pairwise log-ratios (self-normalizing) ws_ratio_image: Create pairwise ratio matrix (CNN input)

what: Isometric log-ratio balances on a frozen partition tree — ws_balance_ilr
title: Isometric log-ratio balances on a frozen partition tree — ws_balance_ilr
text: Computes orthonormal isometric log-ratio (ILR) balances frozen sequential binary partition. partition (G+, G-) balance $$b = \sqrt{\frac{|G+|\,|G-|}{|G+| + |G-|}} \log\!\left(\frac{\mathrm{gmean}(x_{G+})}{\mathrm{gmean}(x_{G-})}\right).$$ default partition (ws_default_sbp) encodes circulating miRNA biology: erythrocyte-vs-rest, platelet-vs-rest, let-7 family within-cluster, miR-17~92, miR-200, miR-371~373, dominant-vs-tail abundance balance computed runtime. Tolerant feature absence: features missing panel simply removed numerator/denominator computation; balance becomes NA either side becomes empty. matrix/data.frame path vectorized deployment throughput. aggregate = "gmean", uses row-wise means logged feature matrix regression-locked prior scalar row-loop semantics, including large "ALL_NON_RBC" / "ALL_NON_PLT" denominators structurally generated SBPs. path also preserves feature names one-column matrices avoids prior multi-column data.frame recursion failure. Backwards-compatibility note: pre-existing "TOP_K_BY_ABUNDANCE" behavior panel size less equal k intentionally preserved frozen within-sample result identity. what: Single-sample miRNA scoring method bank (74 methods)
title: OmicSelector 2.6.0 (2026-07-08)
text: Completed frozen 74-method single-sample scoring bank R/singlesample-*.R, rostered inst/extdata/singlesample_method_manifest.csv enumerable via singlesample_method_roster() / singlesample_method_bank(). Every method single-sample (per-row) scorer: deployed sample scored using panel values plus frozen parameters learned fit time, batch-correction step requirement co-resident reference cohort deployment. Methods carry within (within-cohort) transfer (cross-cohort generalisation) estimand role baseline, discriminator, negative control. bank grouped following families (manifest family codes -O, NC, short grouping letters, descriptive names): Compositional within-sample baselines (family ): trimmed robust-CLR reference (ws_rclr_trimmed, reference, candidate), additive log-ratio frozen pivot pool, MAD log-ratio, panel-internal dominance score pre-analytical-failure detection. Frozen denoisers (family B): frozen-RUV factor removal, robust-PCA residual, robust-regression hemolysis residual removal. Kit-aware compositional transfer scorers (family D): kit-stratified rCLR, kit fixed-effect-adjusted ALR, kit-orthogonal ILR, kit-residual MAD. Anchor/reference denoising transfer scorers (family E): kit-stable-anchor rCLR, hemolysis--kit dual-anchor, RIN-weighted reference scoring. Technology-aware transfer scorers (family F): technology-stratified rCLR, cross-technology harmonised rCLR, technology-residualised ALR. Biofluid-aware transfer scorers (family G): biofluid-stratified rCLR, biofluid-anchor rCLR, biofluid-residualised ALR, blood-cell/platelet marker-exclusion rCLR. Rank / relative-ordering balance methods (family K): k-TSP relative expression ordering (reo_ktsp), pairwise-log-ratio penalised logistic (reo_pairratio), singscore UCell within-sample rank scores, meta-analytic cross-cohort k-TSP (reo_metaktsp), selbal balance selection + log-contrast logistic scorer (bal_selbal), ILR balance scorer (ws_balance_ilr). Likelihood-ratio, optimal-transport, kernel density-ratio scorers (family L): class-conditional likelihood-ratio tests including Bures-Wasserstein (lrt_bw), KDE naive-Bayes (lrt_nbkde), Gaussian-copula (lrt_copula), tail-aware Student-t-copula (lrt_tcopula), vine-copula (lrt_vinecopula, via rvinecopulib), Mondrian-conformal LRT (conf_mondrian), linearised OT embedding frozen reference (ot_lot), sliced-Wasserstein-view Gaussian LRT (ot_slicedlrt), kernel mean-embedding witness (kme_witness), Fisher-Rao geodesic LRT (ig_fisherrao), direct density-ratio uLSIF (dre_ulsif).
